title: Completed reduction towers and stratified perfect local models
statement: For a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme T with l invertible and a finite extension E of Q_l with valuation ring A, an object K of the derived category of modules over the actual completed ring sheaf A_T belongs to the bounded constructible complete reduction-tower category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] if and only if it has a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] with pro-etale locally perfect A-complexes realizing its restrictions. The completed constant realization is exact; the local coefficient rings are the actual inverse images of A_T. No assertion about constructibility of the integral cohomology sheaves is made here. The realization and local-model predicates are precisely [def-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-models].

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11; Definition 6.5.1, retaining uniform reduction models and compatible etale origins.

proof.text: Identify the ordinary integralConstantModule with constants followed by scalar extension along CompletedConstantReduction.base and pbcCompletedComparison. Equality of the scalar maps follows by their finite limit projections. Uniqueness of the tensor/restriction adjunction identifies the composite extension. On a bounded projective representative the K-flat extension counit is invertible; the exact realization factorization identifies integralConstantDerived with the explicit derived-extension model used by perfect-strata-uniform-reductions.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11; Definition 6.5.1, retaining uniform reduction models and compatible etale origins.

proof.text: For stratified perfect K, pull each model sieve back from the chosen terminal object to ProEt.mk(identity), and refine it by a covering presieve. Apply perfect-strata-uniform-reductions to the preceding scalar-extension models. Exact scalar restriction commutes with cohomology, so its common vanishing interval and intrinsic constructible cohomology are precisely PbcUniformReductionProfile.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11; Definition 6.5.1, retaining uniform reduction models and compatible etale origins.

proof.text: On every member of these stratum covers, integral-perfect-chart-complete gives intrinsic completeness for every representative. Map the covering presieves to scheme covers and use stratum-completion-unit-restriction to detect invertibility of the global intrinsic unit. The presentation/intrinsic completeness equivalence in PbcCompletedPullbackActual converts this into PbcIsIntrinsicallyComplete.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11; Definition 6.5.1, retaining uniform reduction models and compatible etale origins.

proof.text: The proved uniform reduction criterion converts the profile into uniform constructible tower models and compatible etale-origin witnesses. Together with the preceding intrinsic completeness, these give membership in PbcIsBoundedConstructibleComplete.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11; Definition 6.5.1, retaining uniform reduction models and compatible etale origins.

proof.text: Conversely, extract intrinsic completeness and the uniform reduction profile from the membership predicates using the same uniform criterion. Its local-effectivity argument supplies a bounded constructible etale presentation of the exponent-one reduction. The chosen uniformizer generates the maximal ideal by the finite-extension DVR theorem; transporting across ULift gives a field structure on the recorded quotient. Apply finite-field-stratified-perfect-models to the etale origin, retaining the finite stratification and all local perfect residue models.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11; Definition 6.5.1, retaining uniform reduction models and compatible etale origins.

proof.text: Each stratum is locally Noetherian by its finite-type immersion and has Noetherian underlying space by the embedding, hence is quasi-compact. Transport the local residue-model isomorphisms across the chosen etale-origin realization isomorphism. Apply integral-residue-stratum-lift independently on each stratum. Its proetale covering sieves and perfect integral models supply exactly IsIntegralStratifiedPerfect, with the same constructible stratification.

G2 Lean assembly: explicit perfect scalar-model comparison, uniform profiles via perfect-strata-uniform-reductions, global intrinsic completeness detection, normalized uniform criterion, finite-field stratification, and two isolated local presentation comparisons. The item theorem is proved from those two strictly local remaining statements; no global equivalent criterion is introduced.

lean.statement:
theorem integralCompletedLocalPerfectCriterion
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] [IsNoetherian T]
    (_hdim : ∃ n : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim T ≤ n)
    (_hl : IsUnit (l : Γ(T, ⊤)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (pbcModules T (pbcAdicCompletion T (pbcIntegralDatum l E)))) :
    PbcIsBoundedConstructibleComplete T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) K ↔
      IsIntegralStratifiedPerfect T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) K
